resumen: Which mode to use and when, without getting confused.

bloques.alt: What you choose in each mode: in Auto, nothing; in P, the ISO; in Tv, the shutter speed and the ISO; in Av, the aperture and the ISO; in M, all three.
bloques.pie: Filled box: you choose it. Empty: the camera chooses it.

bloques.texto: Av if you care about the background. Tv if you care about movement. M when the light doesn't change and you have time.

The dial on your camera decides how much work you do and how much the camera does. There are always three settings that change the photo: [[apertura|aperture]], [[velocidad|shutter speed]] and [[iso|ISO]]. The only thing that changes from one mode to another is which ones you choose and which ones the camera chooses.

items: Auto: the camera decides everything. You don't have to think, but you don't control anything either.
P: the camera chooses the aperture and the shutter speed; you choose the ISO.
[[modo-av|Av]] (A on Nikon and Sony): you choose the aperture, that is, how blurry the background comes out; the camera chooses the shutter speed.
[[modo-tv|Tv]] (S on Nikon and Sony): you choose the shutter speed, that is, whether movement comes out frozen or blurred; the camera chooses the aperture.
[[modo-m|M]]: you choose all three. It is the slowest mode to use.

bloques.texto: Start with Av. It's the easiest mode to learn on: with a single setting you control the background and the camera makes sure the photo comes out neither too dark nor blown out. If what you want is to freeze a movement, like a bird or a wave, switch to Tv and raise the shutter speed.

Move to M when the light doesn't change and you have time: the moon at night with the camera on a tripod, for example. With light that changes fast, like a sunset's, M forces you to keep adjusting the settings and you miss the photo.
Auto is fine too. If there's no time to think or the light changes in seconds, a photo taken is better than a photo missed.
Set the dial to Av and take three photos of the same spot: with the lowest f-number, a middle one and the highest. Compare how much the background changes.
